goal: Accurate match projections. Changed 2026-08-08 from 'find mispriced betting lines'. Judge changes on Brier / log-loss / ECE / CRPS over unseen matches; ROI and CLV are an external benchmark only, never the objective.

resplit_2026_08_08.reason: The original build completed and spent its HOLDOUT on the 2024-01-01..2026-07-20 backtest (2026-07-31). The goal then changed to projection accuracy, which needs an evaluation window never used for selection. Vendor data ends 2026-07-20, so no untouched window existed to promote.
resplit_2026_08_08.cost: HOLDOUT_CUTOFF moved, which constants.py had previously declared permanent. The 2024-2026 backtest is no longer an unbiased out-of-sample estimate for anything fitted after 2026-08-08; it stands only as a description of the frozen original model on data that model had not seen.
resplit_2026_08_08.contamination: The new TUNE, TEST and HOLDOUT were all read once by the original backtest, at aggregate level only (family Brier/ECE/CRPS and ablation totals). No parameter was ever fitted or selected against them and no per-match result informed a decision. Weaker than a selection set, but not zero: report every 2026 number with this caveat.
resplit_2026_08_08.holdout_size: 6,202 raw matches, 2026-01-02..2026-07-20. January-July only, so hard/clay/grass with no fall hard-court season. Down from the original backtest's 24,572.
resplit_2026_08_08.data_defect_found: chall_matches_2024.csv misfiles the 2008 Noumea Challenger (31 matches dated 20071231) under tourney_id 2024-2205, the same id as the real 2024 Noumea. The dates are genuine, not typos; match_num ranges are disjoint (1-31 vs 32-62) so match_id does not collide. data_audit.load_raw now drops pre-DATA_START rows explicitly instead of feeding 2008 matches to Elo. Invisible under the old split because the rows sat inside HOLDOUT.
resplit_2026_08_08.stages_not_refitted: Stages 2-7 are still fitted on data ending 2022-06-30. The re-split widens FIT to 2023-12-31 but nothing has been refitted yet. Any claim that the model was 'retrained on more data' is false as of this entry.
resplit_2026_08_08.tests: 54 split-sensitive tests pass (test_constants, test_data_audit, test_price, test_rules). Four test_data_audit assertions were rewritten to derive from constants instead of hardcoding 2024; the in_scope drift tripwire moved 96,617 -> 114,353.

calibration_refit_2026_08_08.verdict: PASSED on TEST, strictly. All five families improved on ECE, Brier AND log-loss - the criterion the original Stage 8 failed.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.why_run: The shipped maps were fitted on predictions through 2022-06 and never refreshed; match_winner ECE was 0.017 on the original TEST and 0.069 on the original holdout. Separately isotonic put only 7 knots below p=0.20, making the longshot tail a step function fitted on very little data.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.what_changed: model/recalibrate.py gained two map families beside isotonic: PlattMap (2-parameter logistic in logit space, smooth in the tail) and BlendedMap (isotonic in the body, Platt in the tails, baked to a monotone lookup table). fit_maps() takes a method; CalibrationMaps records which was used and still loads pickles written without that field.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.selection: Grid of 3 methods x 4 fitting windows (all/8/5/3 years), fitted on FIT, judged on TUNE. Rule fixed before seeing numbers: ECE decides, log-loss breaks ties and guards sharpness. Selected: blended, 8-year window. Shipped map refit on FIT+TUNE (26,000 matches through 2025-06).
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.tune: uncalibrated ECE 0.0188 -> shipped incumbent 0.0128 -> selected 0.0108. Log-loss flat across the whole grid (0.5627-0.5631 vs 0.5633 baseline), which is the correct shape for a calibration map.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.test_once: 2025-07-01..2025-12-31, 4,133 matches. match_winner ECE 0.0217->0.0181, set_score 0.0122->0.0101, totals_under_high 0.0420->0.0213, totals_under_low 0.0181->0.0160, totals_under_mid 0.0454->0.0336. Brier and log-loss improved for all five as well.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.honesty_note: The grid is a set of near-ties: ECE spread 0.0108-0.0139 on 12,766 TUNE matches, and the window ranking is not monotone (8 beats both all-history and 3). What the evidence supports, in order: recalibrating on recent data beats the stale map; restricting the window helps; which method wins matters less than which window does. Treat blended/8 as the best available choice, not an established fact.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.tail_behaviour: The selected map shrinks longshots LESS than the shipped one (model p 0.20 -> 0.184 vs the old map's -> 0.154). The recent 8 years say the overrating is milder than the 2010-2022 map assumed.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.bug_found_and_fixed: price.py quoted set_betting summing to 1.006. Cause: the shipped map covered only match_winner and totals_under_high, so nothing calibrated set_score; the refit covers all five families, and calibrating each exact set score independently breaks the simplex. Fixed with Pricer._cal_partition(), which renormalises any family whose outcomes partition the sample space - now used by both match_winner and set_betting. Same bug class as the totals over/under/push clamp already in the file.
calibration_refit_2026_08_08.artifacts: model/recalibrate.py, scripts/refit_calibration.py, reports/calibration_refit.md, reports/stage_validations/calibration_refit_test.md, ledger entry stage=calibration_refit

The 17th is a 2025 Tour (other) match; the other 16 are Davis Cup and out of scope.
rules_rebuild_2026_08_08.spec_stability_checked: Regenerating the inferred table over the wider range added 752 keys for 2024-2025 and changed ZERO of the 3,807 existing ones. All 752 are identical to the carry-forward specs rules_for() was already returning, so the calibration refit and its TEST evaluation are unaffected and did not need re-running. holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.status: RUN ONCE, after explicit human go-ahead on 2026-08-09. HOLDOUT 2026-01-02..2026-07-20, 6,202 matches, 126,634 scored selections.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.vs_original_backtest: Original (2024-2026, pre-re-split, old maps): Brier 0.1824, ECE 0.0054, CRPS 3.3800. Pooled ECE improved 0.0054 -> 0.0034. NOT a like-for-like comparison: different window, different sample size, and 2026 is Jan-Jul only.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.THE_HEADLINE: The calibration refit passed TEST cleanly but did NOT fix match_winner on HOLDOUT. match_winner ECE is 0.0665, against 0.0693 for the old maps on the old holdout - essentially unmoved. On TEST (2025 H2) the same map took match_winner ECE from 0.0217 to 0.0181. So match_winner calibrates ~3x worse on 2026 than on the immediately preceding half-year, and this is the SECOND independent holdout where match_winner lands near 0.07 while every distribution family sits under 0.025. Reproducible defect, not noise, and not something a calibration map has fixed in two attempts.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.ablations: full 0.1832/0.0034, no_cohort 0.1832/0.0030, no_venue 0.1833/0.0035, no_corrections 0.1933/0.0363, no_calibration 0.1832/0.0054. Stage 7 corrections remain the only component carrying real weight. no_cohort is marginally BETTER than full on both Brier and ECE - cohort is worthless or slightly harmful on this window, confirming the near-noise-floor gain flagged at the Stage 7 checkpoint. Calibration buys ECE (0.0054 -> 0.0034) at a Brier cost in the fifth decimal, the same trade as the original run.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.provenance_split_is_degenerate_here: documented n=5,568 and Grand Slam n=5,568 are the SAME rows: in the 2026 window every documented-rule match is a Grand Slam. The documented-vs-inferred comparison (0.0176 vs 0.0034) is therefore the Grand-Slam-vs-everything-else comparison relabelled and carries no independent information about provenance. Do not quote it as a provenance finding. Note this reverses the direction seen in the original backtest, which is itself a reason to distrust reading it as provenance.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.caveats: 2026 is Jan-Jul only, so no fall hard-court season. 6,202 matches vs the original run's 24,572. The window was read once by the original backtest at aggregate level, so it is not pristine - see constants.PRIOR_EVALUATION_WINDOWS.
holdout_backtest_2026_08_09.artifact: reports/stage_validations/backtest.md; prior holdout parquet preserved at data/processed/matches_with_holdout.pre-resplit-2026-07-31.parquet

model_vs_market_2026_08_09.question: Under the accuracy goal, how close is the model to the bookmakers as a FORECASTER? De-vigged market probability scored as a rival forecast with the same metrics, on the same matches. No stake, no price, no margin.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.scope: TUNE only (2024-01-01..2025-06-30), ATP main tour, 1,103 matches with joined quotes. The odds file runs to 2026-05 and so covers TEST and HOLDOUT; both are spent, so the script cuts at the TUNE boundary rather than quietly reading them.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.result: market consensus Brier 0.18354 / log-loss 0.54380 / ECE 0.02970; model Brier 0.21522 / log-loss 0.61730 / ECE 0.02027. Gap Brier +0.03168, log-loss +0.07350.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.headline: Against the 0.25 coin-flip baseline the market gains 0.0665 and the model 0.0348, so the model captures ~52% of the market's edge over ignorance. Quote that as the match_winner yardstick.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.the_shape_of_the_gap: The model is BETTER calibrated than the market (ECE 0.0203 vs 0.0297) and WORSE at discrimination. Its probabilities are honest but vague: it cannot separate a 20% match from a 40% match as sharply as a market that also prices injuries, travel and sharp money. The deficit is discrimination, not overconfidence - which is why calibration work has repeatedly failed to close it.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.where_they_disagree: On the 545 matches (half the sample) where model and market differ by more than 10pp: market Brier 0.16509 vs model 0.22561. The market gets SHARPER there. Disagreement is the model missing something, not spotting something - the same conclusion the old betting analysis reached from the other direction (underdog picks claimed +14% edge, returned -8%).
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.caveats: ATP main tour only - OddsPortal carries no Challenger prices, and Challenger is the model's largest and best-calibrated segment (94,468 holdout selections at ECE 0.0041). The gap is probably narrower there but cannot be measured. n=1,103 is modest and it is TUNE.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.all_markets_vs_market: Brier gap to market consensus (positive = model worse), TUNE ATP, pushes excluded, consensus quote per selection: total_sets +0.0039 (n=3,082 sel), total_games +0.0046 (n=25,760), set_betting +0.0075 (n=5,356), games_handicap +0.0186 (n=7,494), match_winner +0.0317 (n=2,206). TOTALS ARE THE MODEL'S STRONG SUIT - roughly level with the bookmakers and BETTER calibrated than them (total_games ECE 0.0200 vs 0.0230; total_sets 0.0174 vs 0.0296; set_betting 0.0101 vs 0.0171). match_winner is the weak one at ~7x the totals gap.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.orientation_tripwire: The handicap result looked like a possible sign-flip in the join (the pricer names 'A +6.5' for A winning BY MORE THAN 6.5, the opposite sign to a bookmaker's -6.5). Checked with a correlation and mean-difference tripwire per market: handicap corr 0.841 with mean difference exactly 0, HIGHER than match_winner's 0.786. The join is correctly oriented and the handicap number is real.
model_vs_market_2026_08_09.FINDING_backtest_handicap_number_is_flat: reports/stage_validations/backtest.md reports handicap ECE 0.0098; against real market lines the model's handicap ECE is 0.0624. Not a contradiction - they measure different lines. backtest.py scores handicaps at FIXED margins (-6.5, -2.5, 1.5, 5.5), and for a winner-oriented row (margin typically +2..+8) the -6.5 and -2.5 rungs are near-certain, so half the scored selections are trivial and drag the pooled ECE down. Bookmakers quote |line| 2.5-8.5, median 4.5, i.e. only where the outcome is genuinely uncertain. TREAT THE BACKTEST'S HANDICAP ECE AS OPTIMISTIC; the model is meaningfully miscalibrated on the handicap lines that actually exist. The same caution may apply to the totals ladder's fixed LINE_OFFSETS, which has not been checked.

split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.verdict: A STRICTLY BETTER SETTING EXISTS. split_sigma 0.09 beats the shipped 0.08 on all four metrics. NOT applied - Stage 7 is frozen and changing it cascades. Measurement only.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.why: The model over-predicts total games by 0.428 (2.218 with Stage 7 off, so the corrections already remove 80% and the mechanism is right). Serve rates explain ~6% of it. split_sigma wobbles the skill split, making sets lopsided and therefore shorter.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.the_numbers: shipped 0.08: bias +0.428, tb_gap -0.0117, pit_dev 0.00707, coverage 0.811. Proposed 0.09: bias +0.119, tb_gap +0.0017, pit_dev 0.00653, coverage 0.820. Better on every one. Beyond that the trade reappears: 0.095 bias -0.042 but pit_dev 0.00780; 0.10 fails the tiebreak gate; 0.12 bias -0.794, pit_dev 0.01677; 0.24 bias -3.055.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.SECOND_AND_MAYBE_BIGGER_FINDING: The shipped 0.08 FAILS Stage 7's own tiebreak criterion on current data: tb_gap -0.0117 against |gap| < 0.01. It passed at -0.0006 when fitted - but that was on the OLD TUNE (2021-01..2022-06). Stage 7 was tuned on a window three years stale and has drifted. This is the same staleness that motivated the calibration refit, and the refit fixed the MAP while leaving the CORRECTIONS underneath it untouched. Retuning Stage 7 is justified by the drift, not by the clever setting.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.selection_rule_note: The script's built-in pick was 'smallest |bias| among gate-passers', which chose 0.095. That is the wrong rule and would repeat the pooled-ECE mistake from the unknown-players work: optimising one metric while the others drift. Stage 7's own rule is minimise PIT deviation subject to the tiebreak and coverage gates, and under that rule 0.09 wins - and happens to dominate outright, so no judgement call was needed.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.reporting_bug_found_and_fixed: Console output and the report's prose printed split_sigma with two decimals, rendering both 0.095 and 0.105 as '0.10'. The markdown table always carried the true values. Format widened to three decimals and the report prose corrected.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.not_applied_because: Changing split_sigma means re-running Stage 7's full gate (not just the three metrics measured here), and the calibration maps sit downstream and were fitted against the current corrections, so they would need refitting too. And there is still no untouched window to verify the result on. Do this as part of a proper Stage 7 re-tune when 2026 H2 data accrues.
split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09.size_of_the_prize: Small. 0.428 games on a mean of 24 is under 2%, and it tightens the totals distribution's centre - which is where the ROI work showed the market is already efficient. A projection-accuracy improvement, not a route to an edge.

totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.verdict: TOTALS NUMBER IS SOUND. The concern raised after the handicap finding does NOT apply to totals. Retracts the suspicion, not the handicap finding.
totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.why_checked: backtest.py scores handicaps at FIXED absolute margins where half the rungs are near-certain, so its handicap ECE 0.0098 is flattered (0.0624 on real market lines). Totals ECE 0.0078 is the headline 'model is good' figure, so it needed the same scrutiny.
totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.result: Totals are scored at offsets from EACH MATCH'S OWN median (LINE_OFFSETS -6.5..+5.5), not fixed absolute values, and that design difference is what saves them. Per-rung base rates on TUNE span 0.064 to 0.740 - no rung is a freebie. Central rungs only (|offset|<=2.5) give ECE 0.02195 against 0.02092 pooled, a 5% difference, versus the 6x gap the handicap check found.
totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.NEW_FINDING_distribution_sits_high: At ALL SEVEN rungs the actual under-rate exceeds the predicted under-rate, by 0.5 to 3.5pp, with no exceptions: predicted 0.0592/0.1759/0.3346/0.4661/0.5743/0.6338/0.7047 against actual 0.0642/0.1848/0.3503/0.4890/0.6015/0.6650/0.7402. Seven out of seven in the same direction is a directional bias, not noise: THE MODEL SYSTEMATICALLY PREDICTS MORE TOTAL GAMES THAN OCCUR - matches finish shorter than it expects. This is a Stage 1/Stage 7 distribution question, not a calibration one, and it explains why totals_under_high was the biggest single gain of the calibration refit (TEST ECE 0.042 -> 0.021): the map is papering over a real shift.
totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.also: ECE rises monotonically with the line, 0.0071 at offset -6.5 to 0.0355 at +5.5, so the model is worst calibrated on high lines.
totals_ladder_check_2026_08_09.two_caveats_on_this_check: The 0.02092 here is UNCALIBRATED while the backtest's 0.0078 has the map applied - they are not comparable and should not be quoted against each other. The 'market line vs model median' part of the script compares per-line values to one global median and is too crude to lean on; the per-rung table is the solid evidence.

totals_roi_2026_08_09.question: Flat-stake ROI betting total games, at prices actually on offer. A BENCHMARK under the current goal, not the objective.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.scope: TUNE only (2024-01-01..2025-06-30), ATP main tour, 81,875 joined total-games quotes. TEST and HOLDOUT not read.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.headline: Betting every positive-edge selection returns -5.01% at Bet365 (n=966) and -3.41% shopping the best of seven books (n=9,690). NO configuration has a confidence interval clear of zero. No demonstrated profit.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.THE_INTERESTING_RESULT: ROI improves MONOTONICALLY as the edge threshold rises, in both books, across all four steps: Bet365 -5.01 / -3.05 / -0.11 / +3.79 at edge >0/2/5/10%, best-price -3.41 / -2.91 / -0.67 / +7.27. The model's edge estimate carries ORDERING information - bigger claimed edge, better result. First market in this project to show that, and a precondition for any selective strategy. Contrast match_winner, where the biggest claimed edges (underdog picks, +14%) were the worst results (-8%): totals behave like a model with signal, match_winner like an overconfident one.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.why_not_actionable_yet: The high-edge cells are tiny (158 bets over 99 matches at Bet365, CI -15% to +23%). Best-price-across-seven-books is fiction - it assumes perfect shopping and ignores limits and account restriction. ~9 correlated selections per match (9,690 bets over 1,090 matches), which is why the bootstrap resamples MATCHES not selections and the intervals are honestly wide. TUNE data with no clean window left to confirm on.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.method_notes: Edge is measured against the RAW price (model_p > 1/decimal_odds), not against the de-vigged probability. That is stricter than the earlier multi_market_clv report, which defined edge against de-vigged market_p and reported -2.69% - the two numbers are NOT comparable (different bet selections, different window, and the calibration map changed in between). Comparing against a de-vigged number counts bets as positive-edge when the actual price is not, which is how paper edges are manufactured. Pushes return the stake and stay in the denominator.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.interpretation: Roughly -3% to -5% flat against a bookmaker margin of about 4-5%. Consistent with the accuracy finding that the model is level with the market on totals: being EQUAL to the bookmaker does not beat the vig, only being better does.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.UNFILTERED_every_match: One bet per match on the PRIMARY line (the most-quoted one), model's preferred side, no edge filter, so observations are independent and the ladder-correlation caveat does not apply. Bet365: n=1,086, ROI -9.27% (CI -14.98 to -3.83, the only interval in this project that excludes zero), hit rate 49.4%, book margin 7.93%. Best price: n=1,095, ROI -2.27% (CI -8.14 to +3.70), hit 50.1%, margin 1.56%. Benchmark is the MARGIN, not zero - blind betting loses the overround by construction. ROI+margin is -1.34pp (Bet365) and -0.71pp (best price), i.e. the model's side selection is slightly WORSE than blind. At mean odds 1.84 breakeven needs 54.3%; the model gets ~50%.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.WHAT_THAT_MEANS_read_with_the_filtered_r: Not a contradiction, and the difference is the finding. The filtered analysis used EVERY rung of the ladder; the unfiltered one uses only the primary line. Together: the MAIN LINE IS EFFICIENTLY PRICED AND THE MODEL ADDS NOTHING THERE. Any edge is confined to the ladder tails - deep overs and unders a book prices lazily because almost nobody bets them. That fits the model's own structure, since the calibration maps were split into totals_under_low/mid/high precisely because tail lines calibrate differently, and it fits the economics of a book pricing its headline number carefully and deriving the rest. REVISES the earlier and too-generous summary that 'the model is competitive on totals and close to profitable'.
totals_roi_2026_08_09.also_worth_noting: Bet365's two-way margin on totals is 7.93%, a steep hurdle. Best-price shopping across seven books compresses it to 1.56%, so most of the apparent gain from shopping is margin compression, not the model performing better.

match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.verdict: DEFECT LOCALISED PRECISELY. Fix found at the Elo layer, does NOT survive the full pipeline. Nothing shipped; stage_3 is untouched.
match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.the_finding: match_winner is not globally miscalibrated. At the Elo layer on all pre-holdout data: both players known n=110,809 ECE 0.0025; match has a debutant n=2,948 ECE 0.0800; layoff 70-140d ECE 0.0314; layoff 140+d ECE 0.0550. The model picks winners excellently between players it knows and is overconfident about players it does not. ~12% of matches carry essentially all the error. That is why no calibration map fixed it (a monotone global map cannot fix a subgroup defect) and why a faster ladder made it worse (K=48 is right for active players).

hypotheses_killed.rating_too_slow: FAILED. Blending a fast-K Elo ladder is monotonically worse at every weight on both log-loss and ECE. reports/form_screen.md
hypotheses_killed.seasonal_january_effect: FAILED. Both test windows were Jul-Dec and both holdout windows opened in January, which looked like a seasonal split. It is not: Jan-Jun ECE 0.0065 vs Jul-Dec 0.0043, nowhere near the 3.7x gap being explained.

match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.fix_built: elo.py gained rank_seed_scale (seed a debutant from ATP rank instead of a flat reference; the rank was in the data, as-of by construction, unused) and the existing inactivity_half_life was gridded. Both default to exactly the current behaviour, and all 14 elo tests pass unchanged.
match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.elo_layer_result: PASSED. half-life 540 + seed scale 160: grouped ECE 0.0241 -> 0.0135, log-loss 0.64729 -> 0.64654, known 0.0214 -> 0.0112, debut 0.1268 -> 0.0683, stale 0.0311 -> 0.0254. All four improve.
match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.end_to_end_result: FAILED. Through the full pipeline on TUNE, uncalibrated: ECE 0.01815 -> 0.02074, Brier 0.23554 -> 0.23561, log-loss 0.66286 -> 0.66301. The Elo-layer gain vanishes and slightly reverses. Stage 4 blends Elo at w=0.80 with serve rates and Stage 7 re-centres to reproduce the uncorrected match-win probability, so the downstream stages - fitted against the OLD Elo - already compensate for exactly the miscalibration this fixes. Fixing it upstream while leaving them fitted to the old behaviour double-counts the correction.
match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.what_would_be_needed: Refit Stage 4 blend weights and Stage 7 corrections against the new Elo, then refit the calibration map, then re-measure. That is a cascade through three frozen stages and a human decision, not something to launch autonomously. The end-to-end number above is a LOWER bound precisely because none of it was refitted.
three_selection_bugs_caught: Pooled ECE as the selection metric rewarded error CANCELLATION: the first run picked a setting whose pooled ECE (0.0062) was better than every one of its own subgroups (0.0108/0.0933/0.0471). Replaced with the size-weighted mean of subgroup ECEs, which can only fall when a group genuinely improves.

The log-loss guard was applied to the argmax instead of as a constraint on the search, so it rejected the whole grid whenever the unconstrained optimum was sharpness-destroying, discarding the settings that satisfied both. Now filter-then-argmax.
First corrected run selected seed scale 160, the edge of the grid. Extended to 240; the selection then sat interior.
match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09.correction_to_an_earlier_claim: An earlier draft said rank_seed_scale was unresolvable because the debut group has only 239 TUNE matches. Too strong. A badly seeded debutant's rating transfers into every opponent they play, so the lever shows up in whole-window log-loss on all 13,293 TUNE matches, where the response is orderly and one-directional. The debut SUBGROUP cannot resolve it; the window can.

latent_hazard_fitted_params_race.what: Every fitting script reads fitted_params.json at start and writes the whole dict at end. Two scripts running concurrently silently drop whichever key the other added in between.
latent_hazard_fitted_params_race.how_it_showed_up: On 2026-08-08 the calibration TEST evaluation clobbered the 'fatigue' key that fit_fatigue.py had written while it ran. fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.verdict: GATE FAILED, twice. Shipped disabled (fatigue.enabled=false). Recorded as a failure, not worked around.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.idea: Rest days, 7-day minutes workload, and qualifier/lucky-loser entry, applied as a logit-space shift to each side's serve-point probability. Coefficients fitted on FIT by maximum likelihood against observed serve points won, gated on TUNE against Stage 2's own two metrics.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.attempt_1: FAILED on a bug of mine, not on the data. rest_days read 0 for 49% of matches because TML records only tourney_date (tournament START), so an entire draw looks like it happened on one day; load7 stacked a week of minutes onto a single date. Diagnosed by checking the feature distribution before reporting the null.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.fix: fatigue.match_day() spreads rounds one day apart from each event's own first round (ROUND_ORDER). Zero-rest share fell 49% -> 4.3%, median rest is now 1 day between consecutive rounds. A self-check pins the round separation.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.attempt_2: FAILED on the data. With correct dates: rest_days -0.0116, load7 +0.0090, is_qualifier -0.0218. TUNE serve-points MAE 0.05964 -> 0.05965, match log-loss 0.66202 -> 0.66225. Neither metric improved; the gate required both.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.what_the_signs_say: The interesting part of the null. rest_days and is_qualifier both came out NEGATIVE, i.e. players with less rest and players who came through qualifying slightly OUTPERFORM their rating. That is a form/survivorship effect, not fatigue: surviving deep into a draw, or winning three qualifying matches, is evidence of current form the 730-day-half-life rate model has not caught up with. Effect sizes are ~0.3pp of serve points across the full feature range, i.e. negligible either way.
fatigue_attempt_2026_08_08.conclusion: Match context as specified carries no usable signal at the serve-point level. Two attempts used, per the loop protocol. A third requires a human decision on direction, not another variant tried autonomously.
options_for_the_human: Accept the null and move on. Cheapest; the evidence says the effect is ~0.3pp at most.

Change the CHANNEL, not the features: apply context to match-win probability directly rather than to serve points. Fatigue plausibly shows up in movement and decisive-point play, which an iid serve-point shift cannot express.
Chase the form signal the signs actually point at (short-horizon form vs the long-half-life rating), which is a Stage 2 recency question, not a fatigue feature.
Drop it permanently and delete model/fatigue.py.

momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.verdict: EFFECT IS SMALL. Point-level momentum is real but tiny; game-level momentum on best-of-three is indistinguishable from zero. Even stacking both at the top of their 95% CIs moves expected total games by 0.053 on a best-of-three - 12% of the 0.428 residual it would have to explain. KEEP THE MIXTURE. Retune split_sigma to 0.09 as already scoped in split_sigma_sweep_2026_08_09. Close this line of work. Nothing was built and nothing shipped: engine.py, corrections.py and fitted_params.json are untouched.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.why_checked: The model over-predicts total games by +0.428 on TUNE. Stage 7's corrections already remove 80% of a +2.218 raw bias and serve-rate bias explains ~6% of the rest, leaving engine.py's iid point assumption as the suspect: it is exact DP over score states with CONSTANT per-point probabilities, so it is Markov in the scoreboard but cannot express history dependence. split_sigma mixes over (pa, pb), which buys static heterogeneity with exchangeable points, not sequential dependence. Momentum and heterogeneity produce the same signature in set scores, so they are NOT identifiable from vendor/ - point-by-point data was the only way to break the tie.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.the_numbers: Point level (P(win serve pt | won prev pt of same game) - P(win | lost it)), debiased: all +0.53pp +/- 0.13, best-of-3 +0.58pp +/- 0.16, best-of-5 +0.45pp +/- 0.22, hard +0.43, clay +0.70, grass +0.78. All p <= 0.05. Game level (P(hold | held prev) - P(hold | broken prev)): best-of-3 +0.10pp +/- 0.36 p=0.78 - ZERO; all +0.45pp +/- 0.31 p=0.13; best-of-5 +1.16pp +/- 0.54 p=0.023. Sizing on best-of-3 at pa=pb=0.64: point momentum -0.011 games, game momentum -0.003, both at the 95% CI top -0.053. Best-of-5 slam, both at CI top: -0.101.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.THE_CONTROL_IS_THE_WHOLE_RESULT: Two confounds, and the second is the one that nearly produced a false finding. (1) Between-player-match heterogeneity: killed with a player-match fixed effect, every statistic computed within a (match, server) unit before aggregating. (2) Miller & Sanjurjo (2018) small-sample bias: within a sequence with the win count fixed, the naive P(W|prev W) - P(W|prev L) is biased downward by exactly -1/(n-1), verified here by enumerating every arrangement for n=10. A player serves only ~10-12 games, so at the GAME level that bias is about -9pp. The raw game-level number is -9.7pp on best-of-three, which looks like a large 'being broken helps you hold next time' effect and is ENTIRELY the artifact - the permutation null is -9.85pp and nothing survives. Every raw point-level number is negative too, and only turns positive after debiasing. A fixed effect alone, without the permutation null, would have reported momentum with the wrong sign.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.FORMAT_DIVERGENCE_worth_remembering: Best-of-five shows real game-level momentum (+1.16pp, p=0.023) where best-of-three shows none (+0.10pp, p=0.78). The holdout is 94% challengers and all best-of-three. Had this been run on the Grand Slam point-by-point data originally specified - all best-of-five - it would have found an effect and generalised it to a format where it is absent. The substituted source containing best-of-three matches is what makes the answer usable.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.direction_of_the_effect: NEGATIVE: momentum SHORTENS matches (streakier holds make sets more lopsided), and the model over-predicts total games, so this is a genuine contribution to the residual rather than a contradiction of it. It is simply about eight times too small to be the explanation.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.DATA_SOURCE_CHANGED_verify_before_reusin: JeffSackmann/tennis_slam_pointbypoint, the source the task named, returns HTTP 404; that account is down to a single public repository. Substituted JeffSackmann/tennis_MatchChartingProject (men's, 2010-2025, 5,384 matches / 876,428 points after the holdout filter). NEW LICENCE CONSTRAINT: MCP is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - attribution, NON-COMMERCIAL, share-alike - whereas vendor/ is MIT. It lives in data/raw/mcp/ (CSVs gitignored, NOTICE committed), is read by this one script, and no MCP-derived number enters fitted_params.json or any shipped artifact. If this project ever becomes commercial, any conclusion drawn from MCP must be re-derived from a permissively licensed source.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.method_notes: Mantel-Haenszel risk difference across units, so a unit with no post-win or post-loss observation contributes zero to numerator and denominator and drops out without an inclusion rule that could depend on the outcome. Standard errors are a sandwich clustered on PLAYER, since the same player appears in many charted matches. P-values are permutation p-values. The point-level null REPLAYS the scoring rule to re-derive game boundaries rather than reusing observed game lengths: a four-point game is WWWW or LLLL by construction, so shuffling inside observed lengths would manufacture the very correlation being measured. 0.6% of point-level units are dropped because the replay does not reproduce their observed game count (retirements, charting gaps). Tiebreaks are excluded, identified as the one game both players serve in rather than by a 6-6 test - the two rules agree on 99.977% of games and the exceptions are NextGen short sets.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.what_was_NOT_separated: Psychological momentum was not distinguished from genuine score-state tactical play (a server plays 40-0 differently from 0-40), and the data cannot distinguish them. Deliberate: both are history dependence the engine cannot express, both would need the same fix, so the measured numbers are TOTAL history dependence and therefore an upper bound on the psychological part. That makes the 'small' verdict stronger, not weaker.
momentum_measurement_2026_08_09.caveats: MCP is crowdsourced and NOT a random sample - it skews to notable matches and top players, and the model's holdout is 94% challengers, so the best-of-three cut narrows but does not close the extrapolation gap. Conditioning on unit length conditions on a stopping time, so exchangeability given (n, k) is an approximation. Game-level units still include truncated final service games from retirements. Simulated rows carry MC standard error ~0.004 games at 2M matches, so table entries under ~0.01 games are zero. Consumed no evaluation window: measured on an external source, nothing fitted, no tune_ledger write, and matches on or after HOLDOUT_CUTOFF are dropped before anything is computed with C.assert_no_holdout enforcing it.

paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.status: SET UP 2026-08-10, not yet started. Nothing has been measured; this entry records what is being tested and what would count as evidence, BEFORE any result exists.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.what_is_being_tested: Whether the frozen model, run forward on matches nobody has seen, produces bets that behave the way the backtests said they would. Two markets only: total_games and games_handicap. match_winner is excluded - it has no edge, and the CLV that once looked positive traced to overrating longshots (match_winner_investigation_2026_08_09).
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.why_the_forward_window_matters: Every evaluation window in this project is spent or contaminated. Vendor data ends 2026-07-20 and holdout_backtest_2026_08_09 read through it. There is no unused window left and re-splitting again is not on the table. Matches from 2026-08-10 forward are the only data no version of this model has seen, and a pick timestamped before the match starts cannot be retro-fitted. That is the entire reason to run this.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.expected_outcome: FLAT TO NEGATIVE PnL, stated in advance so it cannot be reinterpreted later. totals_roi_2026_08_09 found -5.01% flat at Bet365 with no configuration whose CI cleared zero; model_vs_market_2026_08_09 puts the model at ~52% of the market's edge over ignorance and sharper only in calibration, not discrimination. Nothing in the design tries to avoid this.

design.bankroll: 100 units, paper. No bookmaker account exists and no code in the repo can place a real bet.
design.staking: Both schemes run in parallel on the SAME picks so they are directly comparable: flat 2 units per bet, and half-Kelly (0.5 x Kelly x bankroll) hard-capped at 5 units.
design.selection: Edge against the RAW price on offer, not the de-vigged probability - a deliberate deviation from the brief, on totals_roi_2026_08_09's reasoning that de-vigged comparison counts a bet as positive-edge when the real price is not. The de-vigged number is recorded on every row so the looser rule can be evaluated afterwards without re-running anything.
design.one_bet_per_market: A totals ladder's rungs are one correlated cluster; staking all of them would turn one opinion into nine bets.
design.skips: Unknown or ambiguous player, unrecognised tournament, no two-sided quotes, unsupported format, or a pricing failure - the match is skipped and counted. Never filled with a guess.
design.no_clv: Not computed. The OddsPortal scrape carries no Pinnacle, so there is no sharp reference and any CLV number would be noise.

paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.integrity_rules: The ledger (paper/ledger.csv) is APPEND-ONLY: a pick row is timestamped before the match starts, settlement appends a second row, no past row is ever edited. Nothing is tuned on the accumulating results - no mid-run parameter change, no dropping bad days. Changing the staking rule starts a NEW run with a NEW ledger.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.what_would_count_as_evidence: That the chain works forward end to end on unseen data: fixtures resolve, players resolve, matches price, positions settle. An honest count of how often the model can price an ATP fixture at all, and why not when it cannot. A committed timestamped record that later work extends rather than reconstructs. These are process findings and they are the real deliverable.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.what_would_NOT_count_as_evidence: THE PnL. At roughly one or two bets a day the sample will be in the low tens and dominated by variance: a positive PnL is entirely consistent with a model that has no edge, and a negative one is what a model WITH an edge shows reasonably often. Fourteen days on two markets cannot establish the presence or the absence of an edge, and no summary - daily or final - may imply it can. A profitable fortnight is not a reason to bet real money and is not a reason to reopen any closed finding.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.touched: Nothing in the model changed. model/engine.py, model/corrections.py and fitted_params.json are untouched. model/price.py gained one optional argument, history_parquet, so forward pricing can replay history past the holdout cutoff; the default is unchanged and no existing caller behaves differently. scripts/odds_harvester_dynamic.py gained an upcoming-fixtures mode. .gitignore now tracks three files under data/processed/ that the cloud sandbox needs.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.deployment: GitHub Actions on a private repo (.github/workflows/paper-trade.yml), 09:00 UTC cron. Managed Agents was set up first (deploy/paper_trading_deployment.sh, still working) and dropped for cost: it bills per run against API credit and this job does not need an agent. Every money-deciding step is deterministic in scripts/paper_trade.py, which posts to Slack itself; the agent only wrote prose, reconciled unmatched names and flagged odd data, and only the prose is genuinely lost. launchd on the Mac was the other free option and lost because it only fires when the laptop is awake. UNVERIFIED: whether headless Chromium can drive OddsPortal from a GitHub runner - OddsPortal is behind Cloudflare and datacentre IPs are the ones most likely to be challenged. This is the biggest open risk. One manual dry-run must confirm it before the schedule is trusted; launchd is the fallback.
paper_trading_start_2026_08_10.bug_found_during_build: OddsPortal writes a tiebreak set as '7:6 6' or '6 4 :7' depending on who lost the tiebreak, so the tiebreak digit crosses the colon. The obvious regex dropped the second form - a five-setter parsed as four sets and 13 games short, which would have settled totals bets against the wrong number. Caught by the rehearsal path, fixed, and covered by an assertion in scripts/paper_trade.py:demo.

stage_5.notes: Cohort kNN prior replaces the flat tour-average prior for thin players. Style vector: ace rate, DF rate, serve pw, return pw, clay lean, hand, height; features AND standardization stats both as-of the 91-day snapshot (test asserts truncating the future leaves earlier snapshots bit-identical). stage_6.notes: Venue court-speed index, keyed (tourney_code, surface). FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED: multipliers estimated from raw serve-points-won made TUNE total-games CRPS at above-median-history venues WORSE at every setting (baseline 3.8418; best candidate 3.8499, worst 3.8587). Diagnosis: the raw average confounds court speed with field strength - a venue whose draw is full of big servers looks fast. FIX (one attempt, per the loop protocol): estimate the venue effect as a residual, observed serve points won over the model's own expected, so the field cancels. Residual multipliers are tighter than raw (std 0.0062 vs 0.0110, correlation 0.78). GATE PASSED on re-run: CRPS at above-median-history venues 3.8404 vs baseline 3.8418; unmeasured venues unchanged at 3.5880 (they get exactly the surface average, flagged measured=False). Selected shrink_n0=20,000 serve points, indoor flag not in the key (no measurable effect). Gain is small (+0.0014 CRPS); FIT rolling-origin gain mean +0.00149 std 0.00252, TUNE gain +0.00144 - no overfit signal.

stage_7.notes: GATE PASSED on the THIRD attempt. Attempts 1 and 2 are recorded below; the third exceeded the loop's two-attempt limit and was taken under the human's standing /goal directive to continue to completion, after the diagnosis pointed at a fix INSIDE Stage 7's mandate rather than outside it. ATTEMPT 1: one-sided inflation grid could not express the measured gap's sign; nothing moved. ATTEMPT 2: two-sided grid hit its edge at -0.06 and closed 37% of the gap. ATTEMPT 3 (the fix): the variance correction was wobbling the LEVEL. The spec says 'a variance-widening mix over (pa, pb)', and the lever that matters is the SPLIT: a real match's skill gap varies within the match, producing lopsided sets that iid points at a fixed split cannot. The mixture re-solves its centre split so it reproduces the uncorrected match-win probability - without that, wobbling drags every favourite toward even money and destroys the match-winner calibration Stages 3-4 earned. RESULT on TUNE (6,000 matches): tiebreak occurrence gap -0.0817 -> -0.0006 (criterion |gap| < 0.01); total-games PIT deviation 0.02873 -> 0.00697 and central-80% coverage 0.733 -> 0.807 (criterion 0.75-0.85); neither correction degraded the other. Selected: split_sigma 0.08, tiebreak_inflation -0.02 (a DEFLATION - the engine over-predicts tiebreaks on this data, the opposite of the spec's assumed direction), provenance scheme 'pooled'. All three provenance schemes were measured; documented-only has just 483 of 6,000 matches and worse calibration (-0.0229 residual gap). FIT rolling-origin gains: tiebreak +0.07704 +/-0.00925 vs TUNE +0.08117; PIT +0.01756 +/-0.00565 vs TUNE +0.02170. No overfit signal. Both ledger entries frozen. Engine change: match_distribution memoized (the mixture re-evaluates the same triples thousands of times).

stage_8.notes: SHIPPED BY HUMAN ACCEPTANCE, NOT A STRICT PASS. The gate as written required every eligible family to improve on BOTH ECE and Brier. On the replacement TEST window (2023-07-03..2023-11-27, 3,799 matches): totals_under_high improved on all three metrics (ECE 0.0349->0.0110, Brier 0.20895->0.20781, log-loss 0.60852->0.60591); match_winner improved ECE 0.0182->0.0169 but lost 0.0003 Brier (0.23981->0.24013), so the strict verdict is FAILED and reports/stage_validations/stage_8.md still says FAILED. The human reviewed the numbers and chose option A on 2026-07-30: accept, on the grounds that the isotonic map does what it exists for (calibration) and the Brier delta is a sharpness rounding on an already well-calibrated family. No model parameter changed; the saved maps are identical to those a strict pass would have saved. fitted_params.json records gate_strictly_passed=false and shipped_by_human_acceptance=true. Map ELIGIBILITY was decided on FIT+TUNE only, before TEST was opened. TEST touched once per window; the first window (2022-07-01..2023-06-30) is recorded burned in constants.py. The holdout cutoff never moved.

backtest.notes: HOLDOUT BACKTEST RUN ONCE, 2026-07-31, after explicit human go-ahead. Window 2024-01-01..2026-07-20, 24,572 matches loaded, 22,634 scoreable (completed, in scope, clean score, usable serve stats); retirements (863) and suspect scores (127) excluded from scoring and reported separately. BY FAMILY (Brier / ECE): set_betting 0.1711/0.0065, handicap 0.1676/0.0088, totals 0.1885/0.0081, tiebreak 0.2182/0.0091, match_winner 0.2255/0.0693. Match winner is by far the weakest calibration, exactly as MODEL_PROMPT.md predicted; the four distribution markets are all inside 1pp ECE. BY LEVEL: Challenger 0.1852 Brier on 352,946 selections, Masters 0.1745, ATP500 0.1701, Slam 0.1773. BY PROVENANCE: documented-rule matches 0.1773 Brier vs inferred 0.1827 - inferred calibrate slightly worse, the expected direction, which is why provenance was tracked. ABLATIONS (Brier / CRPS): full 0.1824/3.3800; no_cohort 0.1825/3.3809; no_venue 0.1824/3.3812; no_calibration 0.1824/3.3800 (ECE 0.0054 vs 0.0018); no_corrections 0.1929/3.5976. The Stage 7 corrections are the only component carrying real weight on unseen data; cohort and venue are worth ~0.0001 Brier each, matching the near-noise-floor gains flagged at the Stage 7 checkpoint. TWO BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE RUN, both in reporting/plumbing, neither in a fitted component: (1) match_winner and handicap were scored winner-first with a constant outcome, making ECE an artefact (0.4471 and 0.2494); both families are now scored in both orientations and the first report was discarded. Brier and log-loss were unaffected. (2) price.py could quote a total-games price below 1.0 because the isotonic map calibrates `under` alone and could push it above 1-push; the triple is now clamped so over+under+push==1. Backtest metrics are unaffected by (2) - it scores `under` directly and the maps are bounded in [0,1]. Three TML data defects in the 2024+ files also had to be handled: serve counters stored as text, seeds mixing text and numbers, and two Alicante Challengers sharing one tourney_id (555 colliding ids) plus 489 rows with no match_num. 190/190 tests pass.
